newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican stocks race ahead after quiet start.
newsitem.headline: Mexican stocks race ahead after quiet start.

text.p: Mexican stocks raced ahead Wednesday after a quiet first hour on what traders said was a burst of blue chip buying.
At 0955 GMT, the main IPC index was up 1.422 percent or 62.54 points at 4460.36 points. For the first hour, the market had been basically flat.
Traders said the buying was on the back of a market rumor that Standard & Poor's Corp is about to improve its rating of Mexican debt.

"We were almost asleep and suddenly we almost all fell from our chairs. Foreigners stepped in and started buying blue chips," one trader said. "There are rumors that Mexico's debt rating will be raised," he added.
From New York, Standard & Poor's denied the upgrade talk.
"The rumor was that we were going to be upgrading Mexico. That is not true," said David Beers, managing director and head of the sovereign ratings group.
